messages:
li: Heads-up — during q4f16 bring-up of 'orion-lite' we're seeing a consistent detok/translation regression for CJK quotation marks. zh->en BLEU drops ~2.1 on our sanity set and outputs are swapping fullwidth quotes with ASCII and changing spacing.

sophia: example?

li: Short repro:
```
input: 我说：“今天的天气很好。”
hosted (fp16): “Today the weather is great.”
q4f16: "Today the weather is great."
```
Note the model emits ASCII quotes and a preceding colon spacing differs (`说：“` -> `said: "`). That breaks our detok normalization pipeline and downstream diffs.

eva: Interesting — is it purely tokenization or the model learning a different render? Could be a tokenizer/merge change after quantization kernels reorder logits. Any logits dumps?

li: I dumped topk tokens for the token right after the Chinese opening quote. In fp16 the top token is U+201C (LEFT DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK). In q4f16 topk shows U+0022 (ASCII quote) with slightly higher prob. Looks like score crossover at small delta.

marcel: Could be kernel precision noise or softmax temperature shift due to per-group scaling. We saw similar behavior for ideographic comma last quarter.

raj: Can we bisect to a commit? Is this introduced by quantization pipeline change or model remerge?

li: Repro is on the same model artifact before/after quantization conversion. So it's conversion-related. I've filed a tiny repro and attached the token probs. gist: https://git.internal/r/quote-q4f16-probs (private).

marcel: Assigning to me to run a delta-kernel run with exact FP accumulation to confirm. Also going to run the same conversion with fallback scalar softmax to check numeric sensitivity.

sophia: For the eval harness: can we add a focused slice for punctuation/quote orientation so this doesn't hide in coarse BLEU? We should tally exact Unicode diffs too.

li: Agree — current regression alert is on overall BLEU. I'll add a micro-slice "cjk_quotes" with samples from news + chat. Quick numbers: fp16 baseline BLEU 91.3, q4f16 89.2 on the slice.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy orion-lite-q4f16 -> started on canary (3 GPUs) at 2026-03-21T15:02Z :rocket:

eva: Also check detok stage — our normalizer maps U+201C/U+201D to ASCII for en-targets in some downstream steps; that may mask or amplify. We should evaluate both pre-detok unicode-aware and post-detok.

li: Good point. Pre-detok delta is ~2.4 BLEU, post-detok ~1.8. So both matter.

marcel: Quick mitigation idea: during conversion, prefer mapping tokens that are exact unicode punctuation if target-language distribution suggests it. E.g., preserve U+201C token id mapping. But that's hacky.

raj: For release gating, we need an immediate rule: if micro-slice drop >1.0 BLEU and unicode punctuation swap rate >0.5% then fail canary. Can we compute swap rate quickly?

li: Yes — I have a small script that compares token ids around punctuation on the sample set. I'll run it against the canary.

marcel: Running numeric sensitivity test now. If it's just softmax noise, we can try per-channel scaling fix in the converter. If it's quantized embedding insertion, different story.

sophia: FYI @product — this impacts localized UI strings for customers with mixed-script chat. Might be visible in small apps.

eva: Action items: 1) li add micro-slice to eval harness + PR. 2) marcel run numeric sensitivity and post probs. 3) raj block wide rollout if slice BLEU drop >1.0. 4) li run token-swap script on canary and paste results.

li: Will do. Pasting initial token-swap summary: `swap_rate: 0.78% (58/7400 punctuation contexts)` — mostly double quotes and corner-case Japanese quotes.

marcel: Sensitivity test shows softmax peak shifts by ~0.003 in a few positions due to per-group scale rounding; that explains cross-over. Will try converter tweak to preserve high-precision logits for high-entropy punctuation tokens.

raj: Thanks. Keep thread updated. If we need a short rollback playbook, prep a single API route pin to fp16 variant for affected customers.

li: Noted. I'll open the eval PR now and attach canary numbers once deploy finishes.

sophia: :thumbsup:
